--- title: "Two-digit addition and subtraction" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · MATE_ARITM_SUMA_RESTA_2_DIGITOS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_ARITM_SUMA_RESTA_2_DIGITOS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Sumas y restas de dos dígitos*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_ARITM_SUMA_RESTA_2_DIGITOS.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Two-digit addition and subtraction, from age 6 to 8 (1,328 administrations in 4 cohorts). AUC .62–.84 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2258 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 16 (2258) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child makes 8 one/two-digit sums and 8 two-digit subtractions. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:------------------------|:-------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:----------|------------------:| | 2258|Suma y resta - 2 Dígitos |Estímulo y opciones en pantalla | 16| 0|— |— |fijo |Eficiencia | 6, 7, 8, 8.1| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **2258.** 8 sumas y 8 restas. La pantalla muestra la operación con su resultado (formato de verificación), aunque las instrucciones dicen que el niño la resuelve. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![2258 · Suma y resta - 2 Dígitos](../../figuras/plataforma/2258.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2258"} ::: ## Theoretical framework These tasks measure **arithmetic fluency**: solving simple additions and subtractions quickly, above all by retrieving arithmetic facts from memory. There are two formats. In the **production** formats (ages 6–8), the child says the result aloud and the examiner records it. In the **verification** formats (codes 107xx, school year 2021/22), the child sees the operation with a result and decides whether it is correct; they are self-administered and time-limited (60 or 120 s). **What the evidence says:** - **Producing and verifying are not exactly the same.** Production and verification errors are primed separately: verification relies more on the familiarity of the presented result [@campbell1996retrieval]. Scores from the two formats are not interchangeable. - **Arithmetic and reading fluency share predictors.** In 200 Finnish children followed from age 5 to 10, counting and RAN predicted both calculation and reading fluency [@koponen2013counting]. A common factor of RAN and verbal counting was the best predictor of what the two fluencies share [@koponen2020serial]. - **Phonological awareness is associated with fact retrieval, not with procedural calculation.** In 63 children with learning difficulties, phonemic awareness was related to problems solved from memory and not to those that require counting [@matejko2022phonological]. - **Difficulties are persistent and can be anticipated in preschool.** In 2,518 Finnish children followed from Grade 1 to Grade 9, 12% had persistent arithmetic fluency difficulties; preschool counting, number concepts and RAN distinguished this profile [@psyridou2023profiles]. **What our data show.** - **Production.** One-digit additions and two-digit additions and subtractions have acceptable consistency (α = .72–.76). They predict low arithmetic at ages 10–11 (AUC .59–.71) and, to the same extent, low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (AUC .67–.74). The two-digit version has a ceiling at age 7 (23–33% maximum scores) and its screen shows a result, although the instructions ask the child to solve: which format was administered needs to be confirmed. - **Verification.** We do not yet have α for these versions. Their relation with concurrent low reading fluency is moderate (AUC .58–.69). The task for ages 10–11 (code 10748) is itself the low-arithmetic criterion ([Numerical cognition](../../cognicion-numerica.en.qmd#sec-mate-criterio)) and cannot be validated against it. - **Comorbidity.** Of 799 children aged 10–11, 19 have both low arithmetic and low reading, compared with 12.3 expected by chance. Together with the above, this supports a shared retrieval fluency. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 2015| 950|2021/22 | 215| 0| 23| 8| | 7.1| 2012| 899|2019/20 | 223| 219| 0| 14| | 7.3| 2010| 190|2017/18 | 423| 166| 257| 30| | 8.1| 2011| 900|2019/20 | 467| 0| 467| 25| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 7.1| 219| 2012| 12.54| 3.44| 14| -1.20| 0| 23.29| | 7.3| 166| 2010| 13.98| 2.54| 15| -2.07| 0| 32.53| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–16 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 7.1| 219|2.2–16 |1–16 |0–16 | | | 7.3| 166|4.3–16 |2–16 |0–16 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .76. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Reading comprehension (6.2, r = .12); Word and text reading (7.1, r = .55); Word and text reading (7.3, r = .44); Phonological awareness (8.1, r = .45). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .62–.84. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .50–.70. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ARITM_SUMA_RESTA_2_DIGITOS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .67–.74 (2 time points; 132–293 children). Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([provisional criterion](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*), AUC .59–.67. ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 6.2| 215| 2015| 2.0| 4| 5| 6| 9| 12| 14| | 7.1| 219| 2012| 5.0| 8| 9| 11| 14| 15| 16| | 7.3| 166| 2010| 9.2| 11| 12| 13| 15| 16| 16| | 8.1| 467| 2011| 11.0| 12| 13| 13| 15| 16| 16| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ARITM_SUMA_RESTA_2_DIGITOS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 200| -0.214| 0.135| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 213| -0.008| 0.910| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 215| 0.052| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 221| 0.067| 0.322| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 223| -0.322| 0.019| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 223| 0.105| 0.117| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 223| 0.077| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.3| 423| 0.202| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.3| 420| 0.023| 0.811| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.3| 420| -0.014| 0.772| |School (ICC) | 7.3| 423| 0.187| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.1| 466| 0.161| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.1| 467| -0.070| 0.447| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.1| 465| -0.041| 0.378| |School (ICC) | 8.1| 467| 0.106| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Two-digit addition and subtraction” (code 2258; LEEDUCA battery) assesses arithmetic. The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It comprises 16 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 4 sessions, from 6 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .76 (N = 828, 16 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .50–.70. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 7.1, 7.3 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - La puntuación máxima observada (27) supera el número de ítems (16): puede que se puntúen los ítems de ejemplo, que haya una versión con más ítems o un error de datos. Comprobar antes de describir la tarea y distinguir ítems de prueba y de ejemplo. *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
